title: The noisy climb to a threshold

data.source: Euler simulation of ds = v dt + sqrt(2D) dW with a = v = 1, D = 0.05, seeded

prediction: Waits follow the inverse Gaussian law (KS p above 0.01); the counted path grows more than 3 times when white-noise climbs are sampled 16 times finer, and less than 1.1 times with a smooth push.
baseline: The inverse Gaussian first-passage law and ordinary stochastic calculus, which say the same things.
why: Rule R2 is the definition of a first passage, so CRR and the standard model give the same law. The spread of the waits depends on the noise and is not fixed at 0.159. With white noise the count has no settled value.
